topic_summary: Analysis of the Vedic corpus as a commitment system where interpretive authority over unchangeable texts determines the legitimacy of the Varna hierarchy. Orthodox authorities read the texts as literal prescriptions establishing caste as divinely mandated social order, while reformist movements read the same texts as purely spiritual metaphor with no prescriptive social content. The kernel cannot be revised, so all conflict migrates into who has legitimate authority to interpret it.

key_entities: Vedic Corpus (Samhitas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, Upanishads - the textual kernel)
Orthodox Brahminical Authority (traditional interpretive monopoly grounded in birth-lineage)
Reformist Movements (Arya Samaj, Neo-Vedanta, Buddhist-influenced reform - interpretive challenge grounded in ethical universalism)
British Colonial Administration (codified 'Hindu law' via orientalist readings, creating legal precedent)
Indian Constitution (Article 15-17 abolish untouchability, creating legal counter-authority)
key_claims: Orthodox claim: Purusha Sukta (Rigveda 10.90) literally describes cosmic origin of Varna from body parts of primordial being, establishing divine mandate
Reformist claim: Same text is spiritual allegory for cosmic unity, not social prescription
Orthodox claim: Manusmriti elaborates Vedic social order with detailed occupation/marriage/purity rules derived from Vedic authority
Reformist claim: Manusmriti is later interpolation/corruption, not authentic Vedic teaching which emphasized spiritual equality
key_tensions: Birth-lineage authority vs ethical-universalist authority (who has legitimate standing to interpret)
Literal-prescriptive reading vs metaphorical-spiritual reading (what the unchangeable text means)
key_mechanisms: Jati endogamy enforcement (marriage within birth-group maintains social boundaries)
Ritual purity codes (contact/occupation restrictions extract labor value from lower castes)
Educational access control (Sanskrit learning restricted to upper castes, limiting interpretive competition)

axes.selection_reason: Second reading: same kernel, opposite constraint structure; eliminates victim set; metaphorical-spiritual pole of kernel contest

axes.selection_reason: Third reading: external authority imposing interpretive framework; crystallizes fluid practices into fixed legal categories; scaffold type reveals state-building dimension

deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Exits the kernel rather than contesting interpretation; represents authority-rejection rather than reading-contestation; structurally important but outside interpretive-unrevisability frame

omegas.description: Is Manusmriti part of the unchangeable kernel or a revisable elaboration? Orthodox reading treats it as Vedic authority; reformist reading treats it as corruptible commentary. This ambiguity allows interpretive drift to be concealed as textual fidelity.

Does Indian Constitution (Articles 15-17) constitute a new kernel that overrides Vedic interpretive authority, or merely a legal layer that coexists with religious authority in separate domains? If the former, the commitment system has been replaced; if the latter, dual authority structures create ongoing tension.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) - state legal authority as competing kernel

omegas.description: Does translation of Vedic corpus into vernacular languages (post-printing press, post-independence literacy campaigns) constitute kernel revision by changing who can access the text? Orthodox authority claims Sanskrit-only access preserves authentic meaning; reformist movements claim vernacular access reveals manipulated interpretations.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) - linguistic gatekeeping as extraction mechanism

omegas.description: Orthodox reading maps thousands of birth-groups (jati) onto four-fold Varna schema; reformist reading claims this mapping is arbitrary and historically contingent, not textually mandated. The kernel does not specify the mapping, so authority to interpret determines extraction targets.
omegas.source: Extraction mechanism analysis - ambiguity in victim identification

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Topic genuinely instantiates contested kernel structure: one shared textual commitment (Vedic corpus as authoritative), multiple incompatible readings (literal-prescriptive vs metaphorical-spiritual vs colonial-administrative), readings emit structurally different constraints (high-epsilon snare vs low-epsilon rope vs state-building scaffold). Dalit Buddhist reading exits the kernel entirely, representing authority-rejection rather than reading-contestation, appropriately deferred.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The Vedic corpus (Samhitas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, Upanishads) as unchangeable sacred texts whose authority all parties accept but whose meaning is contested
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Orthodox: birth-lineage Brahminical monopoly on Sanskrit learning and ritual interpretation. Reformist: ethical universalism and textual-critical scholarship. Colonial: administrative codification backed by state power. Constitutional: legal framework overriding religious authority.

readings.commitment: Vedic texts literally prescribe Varna hierarchy as divinely mandated cosmic order
readings.authority_grounding: birth-lineage Brahminical interpretive monopoly grounded in ritual purity and Sanskrit access control
readings.expected_structural_delta: High-epsilon snare: Shudra/Dalit castes enter victim set; occupational/marital/ritual restrictions extract labor value and enforce social boundaries; beneficiary is Brahmin caste

readings.commitment: Vedic texts describe spiritual unity and metaphorical cosmology with no prescriptive social content
readings.authority_grounding: ethical universalism, textual-critical scholarship, appeal to Upanishadic non-dualism as 'true' Vedic teaching
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low-epsilon rope: no victim set; Varna reinterpreted as symbolic or abolished as corruption; coordination cost is low (spiritual practice compatibility); no extractive mechanism

readings.commitment: Vedic/Dharmashastra texts constitute unified, timeless 'Hindu law' system to be codified for administrative governance
readings.authority_grounding: British colonial state power backed by orientalist scholarship claiming superior textual objectivity
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate-epsilon scaffold: crystallizes fluid social practices into fixed legal categories; creates legible subjects for census/taxation/adjudication; beneficiary is colonial administration; victim set includes all colonized legal subjects subjected to codified caste law

axiom_contradictions.basis: Orthodox axiom: textual prescription determines social legitimacy (birth-caste is divinely mandated reality). Reformist axiom: ethical universalism determines social legitimacy (birth-caste is illegitimate discrimination). No single framework can hold both 'divine mandate legitimizes hierarchy' and 'ethical equality delegitimizes hierarchy' simultaneously.

Colonial axiom: textual stability enables legal codification (unified timeless 'Hindu law' exists). Reformist axiom: textual plurality enables ethical reinterpretation (Vedic teaching is diverse and evolving). No single framework can hold both 'texts are fixed and unified for legal purposes' and 'texts are plural and revisable for ethical purposes' simultaneously.
